fix round 2 rule: Design decision (Planner): context_router.cache_mode(cfg, section) goes back to a pure accessor that returns the validated configured value (existing tests in tests/test_pool.py and tests/test_spawn.py pass unchanged). The promotion gate lives in a new context_router.effective_cache_mode(cfg, section, *, root, now=None, remembered=None) -> (mode, refused_reason): it calls cache_mode, and only when the configured value is active it calls promotion.evaluate(feature, promotion.collect(feature, root), cfg, root=root, now=now) and returns shadow with the stay reason; it is called once per packet build at the three entry points in spawn.py (context, tools, skills) with root=STATE, never from the accessor; the decision rows record configured_cache_mode, effective cache_mode and refused_reason so a refused active is visible in the log and scorecard; notify fires only when the refusal reasons change (kept on the pool object like steering) and is wrapped so a failure never breaks spawning; an unknown section raises ValueError, never KeyError. Move the acceptance test test_cache_mode_active_refuses_to_shadow_when_promotion_stays onto effective_cache_mode. Docs 19 gain a revert note: git revert of this task's commits restores ungated active.
Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until it exits 0; do not ask questions; report files changed and failures-only output.

Move the acceptance test test_cache_mode_active_refuses_to_shadow_when_promotion_stays onto effective_cache_mode. result.summary: The gate lives in effective_cache_mode as designed, but it does not cover all packet entry points and it fails open in one case. I read the T-1325 diff against 27bdb30 and the surrounding spawn.py code. I did not run the tests. Note: the packet's base sha de0ee77 equals HEAD, so the packet's own diff is empty.

comments.issue: Fail-open: when root is None, evaluate() appends eval_root_missing but then filters it out of the blocking reasons, so the fresh Hermes eval check is skipped and the feature can return promote. Activation must be refused without a fresh eval. Treat eval_root_missing as blocking.

The gate only runs inside packet() and review_packet(). run_worker calls _shadow_tool_disclosure(t, role, pool.cfg, ...) with the raw config. For scout and spec_review roles, scout_packet and spec_review_packet never call _packet_cache_config, so t['_cache_decisions'] is unset. A configured active cache_mode is not gated for those roles, and tool_catalog.cache_fields still reads the raw active value. The spec requires one gate at each of the context, tools and skills entry points.

_packet_cache_config runs promotion.evaluate and promotion.collect for three sections on every packet build when active. Each call reads the whole decision log, the tasks directory and the scorecard. Only ValueError is caught, so any other error from collect or evaluate breaks spawning. The decision_log.record calls in the same function are also unguarded. Wrap the evaluation and the recording in a failure-safe try.

The function writes task['_cache_decisions'] and the shared module-level _CACHE_NOTIFICATION_POOL, which is a mutable Pool created once and shared across threads. The private key can leak into a persisted task dict or into hashing. If pool is None, notification memory is also process-global.

Existing memory_tiers behaviour changed. Regressions now only stay for that feature, and a new early demote path uses active_n>=10. The acceptance criterion says existing features are unchanged apart from additive criteria. The hunk at line 234 hard-codes feature != 'memory_tiers'.

The evidence counts gate rows, one per packet build across execute, review and fix rounds, not per task. min_shadow_samples of 30 can be met by about 10 tasks. Because every configured non-off build is logged as a gate row, refused-active builds count as shadow evidence for their own promotion.
